content.text: The issue is a module name mismatch: `build.js` is trying to require `./lib/greeting`, but the actual file is named `./lib/greet.js`. I'll fix this with a minimal change:

content.content: The file /work/project/build.js has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This was a path resolution error – the most common source of module-not-found failures in Node.js. When `require()` can't locate a module, it looks for the exact path provided relative to the current file. Since the actual file was `greet.js` but the require statement referenced `greeting`, the module resolver couldn't find it. This type of mismatch typically happens after file renames or when import paths diverge from their actual targets.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

SWITCHYARD: fixed
